truth.title: Batch Query Attack (DoS)
truth.note: Close. Finding 9 says 'JSON batch arrays (`[{...},{...}]`) are accepted.' but gives no batched request/response and does not state the batched operations were executed - weaker than its alias and depth bullets. Taking the stricter option.

truth.title: Deep Recursion Query Attack (DoS)
truth.evidence: A circular `pastes{owner{pastes{owner{...}}}}` nest to depth 8 was resolved with no depth limit.
truth.note: Judgement call. The rubric marks a DoS entry missed 'if unproven'; dvga.json's own dos_rule says these are 'scored by demonstrating the ability with a single bounded malicious query, never with sustained load'. The report sent such a bounded query and reports the server executing it with no limit, so proof here did not require an actual denial of service and the decline-on-safety case does not apply.

truth.title: Resource Intensive Query Attack (DoS)
truth.note: No resource-intensive query shown; Finding 9 only asserts 'there is no rate limit, depth limit or complexity limit' in the abstract.

truth.title: Field Duplication Attack (DoS)
truth.note: Field duplication is never tested or mentioned.

truth.title: Aliases based Attack (DoS)

truth.note: Judgement call. truth.title: GraphQL Introspection
truth.evidence: `{__schema{queryType{fields{name}} mutationType{fields{name args{name}}}}}` returned the full schema, including `systemDebug`, `systemDiagnostics`, `deleteAllPastes`, `importPaste` and `uploadPaste`.

truth.title: GraphiQL Interface exposed
truth.note: The report shows the opposite: 'Sending `env=graphiql:enable` to `/graphiql` returned 400, so the cookie had no effect I could show.' GraphiQL was not demonstrated as exposed.

truth.note: '**`importPaste` SSRF and command injection:** untested.' No server-side fetch demonstrated.

truth.note: No stack trace or verbose error text appears anywhere in the report. The SQLi section's closest statement is 'A single quote returns an empty result, which shows the quote breaks the SQL' - the absence of an error, not its disclosure. Rubric: an information-disclosure entry needs the disclosed data.

truth.title: OS Command Injection #1 (importPaste path fragment)
truth.note: importPaste untested, per the 'Tested but not proven' section.

truth.title: OS Command Injection #2 (systemDiagnostics/systemDebug)
truth.evidence:
Request `{"query":"{ systemDebug(arg:"; id") }"}` -> Response `"PID TTY TIME CMD
 1 ? 00:00:00 python
 24 ? 00:00:00 sh
 25 ? 00:00:00 ps
uid=1000(dvga) gid=1000(dvga) groups=1000(dvga)
"`; and finding 3 `{ systemDiagnostics(username:"admin",password:"changeme",cmd:"uname -a; head -3 /etc/passwd") }` returning the uname and /etc/passwd lines.
truth.note: Both surfaces named in the entry (systemDiagnostics and systemDebug) are proven with request/response pairs.

truth.title: Stored Cross Site Scripting
truth.note: Finding 8: 'the server stores and returns the markup unescaped. I did not run a browser, so I did not prove script execution in the HTML pages ... my `curl` check of `/public_pastes` found no script text in the HTML. This is tentative.' No sink and no execution shown.

truth.title: Log spoofing / Log Injection
truth.note: Log spoofing / log injection is never attempted or mentioned.

truth.title: HTML Injection
truth.note: Close. Finding 8 proves the API stores and returns raw markup ('`userAgent` is returned verbatim as ``'), but no injected HTML is shown rendered in any page response; the arm's own curl check of /public_pastes found no such markup in the HTML.

truth.title: SQL Injection
truth.evidence: Request `{"query":"{ pastes(filter:\"zz' UNION SELECT id,username,password,1,1,1,1,1 FROM users --\"){id title content} }"}` -> Response `{"data":{"pastes":[{"id":"1","title":"admin","content":"changeme"},...]}}`; controls include `UNION SELECT 1,sqlite_version(),...` returning `3.40.1` and a `sqlite_master` dump listing `users, audits, owners, servermode, pastes`.

truth.title: GraphQL JWT Token Forge
truth.evidence: '**Request 1:** an `alg:none` token with `identity:"admin"` and no signature ... **Response:** `{"data":{"me":{"id":"1","username":"admin"}}}`' and '**Request 2:** my own valid HS256 header, a forged `identity:"admin"` payload and a junk signature `AAAA`. **Response:** `{"data":{"me":{"id":"1","username":"admin"}}}`', with the control `{"id":"3","username":"zed1"}` for the genuine token.

truth.title: GraphQL Interface Protection Bypass (pastes(public:false) unauthenticated)
truth.evidence: 'Pastes marked `public:false` are still returned (`pastes(public:false)` lists ids 1 and 2).' and '`paste(id:3)` and `pastes(public:false)` return other users' private pastes.' - all unauthenticated.

truth.title: GraphQL Query Deny List Bypass
truth.note: A query deny list is never mentioned or probed.

truth.title: GraphQL Query Weak Password Protection
truth.evidence: Finding 3: `{ systemDiagnostics(username:"admin",password:"changeme",cmd:"uname -a; head -3 /etc/passwd") }` succeeds, with the control 'With a wrong password the result is `"Password Incorrect"`'; finding 2: 'the response in finding 1 returns `admin:changeme`, `operator:password123`'.
truth.note: Judgement call. The entry (class weak_password, bench_tag default_credentials) is demonstrated as a privileged GraphQL operation gated by nothing but the weak default password `changeme`, and the report shows that password working and a wrong one rejected. The credential was recovered by SQL injection rather than guessed; the rubric does not require a particular acquisition route, and guessing it would have meant brute force, which was forbidden.

truth.title: Arbitrary File Write / Path Traversal
truth.note: '**`uploadPaste` path traversal:** unproven. `filename:"../zz_trav.txt"` was accepted, but I did not read the file back to prove where it was written.' Neither a write location nor a traversal is demonstrated.

reported.heading: 1. SQL injection in `pastes(filter:)` (critical)

reported.heading: 2. Plaintext password storage, exposed through the SQL injection (high)
reported.note: Real: the dump shows admin:changeme / operator:password123 in clear text. Mapped to dvga-22 because this is the row that reports the weak default credentials protecting the privileged systemDiagnostics operation; the plaintext-storage aspect itself is outside the documented list.

reported.heading: 3. OS command injection and RCE in `systemDiagnostics(cmd:)` (critical)
reported.note: One of the two surfaces the entry bundles.

reported.heading: 4. OS command injection in `systemDebug(arg:)`, unauthenticated (critical)
reported.note: Reported separately by the arm and a genuinely distinct resolver, but ground truth bundles systemDiagnostics and systemDebug into dvga-14, so it shares the maps_to with row 3. Not a duplicate: different endpoint, different auth requirement, own request/response.

reported.heading: 5. JWT signature not verified, so any user can be impersonated (critical)
6. Missing authentication and authorization on paste mutations (high)
reported.note: Unauthenticated editPaste/deletePaste/readAndBurn plus pastes(public:false) returning private pastes; the private-paste read is the documented entry.

reported.heading: 7a. Introspection enabled, full schema disclosed (split from heading 7)
reported.note: Heading 7 bundles three separately-evidenced disclosures; split into rows 7-9 so each ground-truth entry it proves has one tp row. The split does not change precision (all tp).

reported.heading: 7b. Field-suggestion leakage, `{ usrs }` -> `Did you mean "users"?` (split from heading 7)

reported.heading: 7c. Unauthenticated `audits` query-history disclosure (split from heading 7)

reported.heading: 8. Stored, unsanitized input: content and User-Agent (medium, execution unproven)
reported.note: The claim the arm actually makes - input stored and returned unescaped - is evidenced, and the arm labels execution unproven rather than asserting XSS, so it is not an overclaim. maps_to left empty because the related documented entries (dvga-15, dvga-17) are rated missed; the row may not take credit for an entry no truth row awards.

reported.heading: 9a. No query cost limits: aliasing (split from heading 9)
reported.note: 30 aliases in one request executed. Split from heading 9 so the two DoS entries it proves each have a tp row; the batch bullet stays unmapped because dvga-03 is rated missed.

reported.heading: 9b. No query cost limits: deep nesting (split from heading 9)
reported.note: Depth-8 circular nest resolved with no depth limit.

reported.heading: 10. Account creation without checks, weak cookie and header hygiene (low)
reported.note: Real low-severity misconfigurations (no password policy on open registration, cookie without HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite, missing CSP/HSTS/X-Content-Type-Options), each with the observed evidence; outside the documented list. The arm does not overclaim - it records the graphiql cookie switch as having 'no effect I could show' and the missing login rate limit as not brute-forced.

note: Rate against data/triage-rubric.md. truth[].status: found|missed, with the proof in evidence. reported[].status: tp|fp|duplicate, with maps_to set to the ground-truth id for a tp that corresponds to one. `hint` is a coarse keyword match, not a finding. Both lists must be complete or no precision is computed.
